summary:
R4 is the model to lean on today. Its 14-day strong-play window is 44-28 (61%, +14.0u, n=72) and its SP and bullpen categories are both riding 6-game win streaks, with SP at 55% (14d) on top of a 57% season mark and bullpen actually improving to 56% over the last two weeks versus 54% season-long. The one blemish is R4's runs category, cold with a 3-game losing streak and sitting at just 48% over 14 days — worth discounting anywhere R4 splits from the pack. That's exactly what happens twice today: ARI @ KCR and HOU @ PHI. In KCR, R1/R2/R3 all like the Royals while R4 breaks off to Arizona (-0.44) — with runs currently R4's weak spot, side with the trio on KCR. Same story in Philly: R1-R3 lean Houston while R4 flips to Philadelphia; trust the consensus, especially with PHI a profitable strong-play team this season (12-6, +4.0u) and BOS/LAD/TBR-style favorites making R4's outlier look more like noise than signal.

Everywhere else today, all four ratings agree, and the deltas are loud. NYY over COL is the day's biggest consensus (R4 +2.29, R3 +2.00), and LAD over CIN is right behind it — LAD as a picked team is money this year at 29-13 (69%, strong 21-4, +23.0u), so this is about as clean as the model gets. SDP over WSN, TOR fading in Oakland, and PIT fading into Chicago's south side all show tight agreement across R1-R4 with deltas beyond 1.0, historically the strong-play threshold that's produced R3's 58% (14d, +6.0u) and R4's 61% hit rates. Categorically, trends+sp remains the top combo agreement at 57.0% (n=523), and with SP hot across every rating today, games like NYY, LAD, and MIL where pitching mismatches are stark (Gausman/Henderson, Yamamoto) are where that combo should hit hardest. Treat CLE@BAL and TBR@ATL as secondary consensus plays — real signal, just smaller magnitude.
